See how Red Hat Lightwell transforms open source vulnerability remediation from a weeks-long manual process into an automated operation.
In this walkthrough, follow Dinesh, a Platform engineer at a fictional financial services company, as he arrives to find that Lightwell has already processed 298 patches across 29 applications — analyzing CVEs, assessing risk against business criticality, generating merge requests, and auto-merging the safe ones — leaving only a handful flagged for his expert review.
The demo showcases an end-to-end remediation pipeline spanning multiple Red Hat technologies: Lightwell Network delivers remediated binary packages, an AI-powered agent on OpenShift AI assesses risk and generates merge requests in GitLab, Trusted Profile Analyzer validates SBOMs, Event-Driven Ansible orchestrates the workflow, Trusted Software Factory builds and signs container images, and Advanced Cluster Management with GitOps deploys the patched applications across a multi-cluster fleet.
Together, these components demonstrate how enterprises can shift from reactive patching to continuous, policy-driven remediation at scale.

What Gets Deployed
* A per-tenant OpenShift namespace with a personal Keycloak login
* The Lightwell all-in-one demo application, running as a single pod and exposed via a Route
